engine: Local Python numpy/scipy sandbox; reproducible policy assumptions documented in docs/game-design/12-SIMULATION-INFLUENCE-COLONISATION.md
city_influence_model: most radii 1-3, 4-5 infrequent, 6 exceptional; explicit military opportunity-cost represented by city quality/age proxy; not genuine upkeep troop allocation
outside_influence_cost_hypothesis: base=1+0.42*(cities_owned-1)^1.35; cost=base*(1+0.37*d+0.08*d*d), d=distance beyond nearest allied city influence; parameters provisional
note: No definitive saturation forecasts; allowed expansion selects cheapest admissible cells and biased towards allied influence. The initial player spawn spreads positions evenly, strongly reducing early rival contacts.
readout: At three cities per player and modest influence radius, 300-500 cells/player fails to create meaningful alliance borders in this model. 120-180 cells/player brings first measurable rival contacts, but 10-city viability and long-run balance remain untested.
cautions: Model lacks troop power, S2 upkeep formula, real influence growth/decay, siege and capture, total 10-city late game, dynamic territorial ownership and alliance-focused placement.

Distance cost sensitivity run with/without penalty yielded same results in sampled settings because simulated budgets/candidate placement were not constraining; therefore no estimated causal effect of the cost curve.
Late-game friction forecast cannot be inferred from these runs.
